question_text: A 62-year-old man with history of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and COPD presents to his cardiologist for a right heart catheterization procedure after a recent echocardiogram revealed pulmonary artery pressure (PAP) of 55 mmHg. Intraoperative administration of intravenous adenosine causes the PAP to decrease to 35 mmHg. What pharmacological therapy is most likely to provide long-term benefit for this patient?
